page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-8 is an Arm-based compute instance built on a 64-bit Arm architecture (arm64). The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage volumes, necessitating network-attached persistent disks for storage needs, and includes zero GPU accelerators.

The 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes compute throughput over memory density. Arm64 processors offer high instruction efficiency and lower thermal requirements, which translates to a favorable cost-efficiency profile for CPU-driven tasks compared to traditional x86 designs. However, architectural tradeoffs include strict memory constraints per thread and the prerequisite of Arm64-compatible software stacks. The lack of integrated NVMe or local storage also makes the server dependent on external network throughput for IOPS-heavy operations.

Given its hardware profile, Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-8 is suited for compute-bound applications that do not require substantial resident memory. Typical deployments include web servers, microservice APIs, software compilation, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) runners, batch data parsing, and horizontally scalable container workloads.
